title: WHO publishes its first global guidelines on obesity in children and adolescents
body: The World Health Organization has issued its first global guidelines on managing obesity in children and adolescents. It strongly recommends structured support on diet, physical activity and behaviour. It advises against medicines, weight-loss surgery and devices for children under 10, and says approved medicines for ages 10 to 19 should be considered only if a supervised lifestyle programme has not worked.

source.title: WHO issues first global guidelines on child and adolescent obesity

title: New global roadmap targets high blood pressure in pregnancy
body: WHO says high blood pressure disorders affect an estimated 10 to 15 percent of pregnancies and cause about 16 percent of maternal deaths worldwide, roughly 42,000 a year, and are linked to more than 500,000 stillbirths and newborn deaths annually. The new roadmap covers 2026 to 2035 and beyond, and focuses on research, clinical guidance, access to medicines and diagnostics, putting plans into practice, and accountability.

source.title: New global roadmap launched to tackle hypertension in pregnancy, a leading cause of maternal and newborn deaths

title: WHO urges countries to move from long-stay psychiatric hospitals to community care
body: WHO has released a practical guide to help countries shift away from long stays in psychiatric hospitals towards person-centred care in the community, a process called deinstitutionalization. It says nearly half of the people in these institutions are held involuntarily, sometimes for years, and that only 9 percent of reporting countries have fully moved to community-based care.

source.title: WHO urges shift from institutional to community-based mental health care

title: UN chief warns biodiversity protection is off track ahead of COP17
body: Speaking in Yerevan, Armenia, ahead of the UN biodiversity conference, the UN Secretary-General said that even if countries meet their current commitments, only 26 percent of land and 12 percent of the ocean would be protected by 2030, short of the 30 percent goal. He also said biodiversity finance is less than half of the 200 billion dollars agreed under the global framework.

source.title: Guterres urges faster action and financing to stop biodiversity loss

title: UN ocean assessment: sea-level rise has doubled and over a third of fish stocks are overfished
body: The UN's World Ocean Assessment, compiled by about 550 experts from 86 countries, reports that sea-level rise has roughly doubled, from up to 1.9 millimetres a year before 2015 to 4.3 millimetres in 2023. It says oxygen-poor dead zones now cover about 4.5 million square kilometres, and that 37 percent of fish stocks were overfished in 2021.

source.title: Humanity's future depends on protecting the rapidly changing ocean

title: Press freedom group: four more journalists detained in Turkey under the disinformation law
body: The Committee to Protect Journalists says four journalists were arrested or placed under house arrest over a weekend on suspicion of spreading disinformation, and that at least 22 journalists have been arrested or detained under the law this year. It called for everyone held to be freed immediately and for the law to be abolished.

source.title: Turkey: 4 more journalists arrested for 'spreading disinformation' as media crackdown intensifies

title: UN agency warns internet shutdowns are rising worldwide
body: UNESCO says governments imposed at least 300 internet shutdowns across more than 54 countries over two years and, citing the monitoring group Access Now, that 2024 was the worst year since 2016. A 2022 UN human rights office report found that shutdowns rarely meet international standards of legality, necessity and proportionality.

source.title: UN warns of rising internet shutdowns as digital blackouts spread worldwide

title: UK reports on its open contracting reforms a year after the Procurement Act
body: The UK government's final status update says the Procurement Act 2023 came into force on 24 February 2025 and that a central digital platform for tenders launched the same month, with more than 90,000 registered users by December 2025. Work on a data strategy and a civil-society open contracting community continues in 2026.

source.title: UK NAP6 final status update commitment 1: open contracting

title: Analysis: UK direct contract awards fell, but few contracts report performance data
body: The Open Contracting Partnership's analysis of the first year of UK procurement data found the share of direct, uncompetitive procedures fell from 53 percent in March 2025 to 34 percent in February 2026, while open tenders rose from 27 to 41 percent. Only 4.7 percent of contracts in the dataset include performance metrics, rising to 28 percent for contracts above 5 million pounds.

source.title: The UK Procurement Act one year on: what does the data tell us?

title: Security researchers: npm attacks are growing and moving into build pipelines
body: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 describes the September 2025 Shai-Hulud worm as a turning point, with more frequent and more sophisticated attacks on npm since. It reports attackers moving into CI/CD pipelines, in one May 2026 campaign publishing malicious packages with valid provenance, so provenance checks alone are not enough. Suggested steps include delaying very new package versions by 24 to 72 hours, disabling install scripts, and using lockfiles with npm ci.

source.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations
